title.en: Number Representation: Binary, Two's Complement and IEEE 754
title.ru: Number Representation: Binary, Two's Complement aur IEEE 754

subject: Computer Architecture

intro.en: Inside the CPU everything is bits. How integers, negative numbers and fractions are encoded decides the range of values a computer can store and how arithmetic works.
intro.ru: CPU ke andar sab kuch bits hai. Integers, manfi numbers aur fractions kaise encode hote hain, isi se tay hota hai ke computer kitni range ki values rakh sakta hai aur hisaab kaise hota hai.

definition.en: Unsigned integers are stored in plain binary. Signed integers use two's complement: a negative number -x is stored as (invert the bits of x) + 1, giving the range -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1) - 1 for n bits. Real numbers use IEEE 754 floating point: sign, biased exponent and fraction (mantissa).
definition.ru: Unsigned integers saade binary mein rakhe jate hain. Signed integers two's complement istemal karte hain: manfi number -x ko (x ke bits ulat kar) + 1 rakha jata hai, jis se n bits mein range -2^(n-1) se 2^(n-1) - 1 tak hoti hai. Real numbers IEEE 754 floating point istemal karte hain: sign, biased exponent aur fraction (mantissa).

explanation.en: Each hexadecimal digit is exactly 4 bits, so 1011 0110 = 0xB6. Two's complement makes addition and subtraction use the same circuit, has a single zero and its most significant bit shows the sign. Overflow happens when the result does not fit: adding two positive numbers gives a negative result or vice versa. Sign extension copies the sign bit when widening (8-bit 1111 0011 = -13 becomes 16-bit 1111 1111 1111 0011). IEEE 754 single precision has 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127) and 23 fraction bits; value = (-1)^s x 1.fraction x 2^(exponent - 127). Double precision uses 1, 11 (bias 1023) and 52 bits. Many decimals such as 0.1 cannot be represented exactly, which is why 0.1 + 0.2 is not exactly 0.3.
explanation.ru: Har hexadecimal digit bilkul 4 bits hai, is liye 1011 0110 = 0xB6. Two's complement jama aur tafreeq ke liye ek hi circuit istemal karta hai, is mein ek hi zero hota hai aur sab se ahem bit sign batata hai. Overflow tab hota hai jab natija samaa na sake: do positive numbers jama karne se manfi natija aaye ya is ka ulat. Sign extension width barhate waqt sign bit copy karti hai (8-bit 1111 0011 = -13, 16-bit mein 1111 1111 1111 0011). IEEE 754 single precision mein 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127) aur 23 fraction bits hain; value = (-1)^s x 1.fraction x 2^(exponent - 127). Double precision 1, 11 (bias 1023) aur 52 bits istemal karta hai. 0.1 jaise kai decimals bilkul durust nahi ban sakte, isi liye 0.1 + 0.2 bilkul 0.3 nahi hota.

example.en: -13 in 8-bit two's complement: 13 = 0000 1101, invert = 1111 0010, add 1 = 1111 0011 (0xF3). 5.75 in IEEE 754 single precision: 5.75 = 101.11 (binary) = 1.0111 x 2^2; sign 0, exponent 2 + 127 = 129 = 1000 0001, fraction 0111 followed by zeros; bits 0 10000001 01110000000000000000000 = 0x40B80000.
example.ru: -13 ko 8-bit two's complement mein: 13 = 0000 1101, ulat = 1111 0010, 1 jama = 1111 0011 (0xF3). 5.75 ko IEEE 754 single precision mein: 5.75 = 101.11 (binary) = 1.0111 x 2^2; sign 0, exponent 2 + 127 = 129 = 1000 0001, fraction 0111 aur baqi zero; bits 0 10000001 01110000000000000000000 = 0x40B80000.

title.en: Instruction Set Architecture and the Instruction Cycle
title.ru: Instruction Set Architecture aur Instruction Cycle

subject: Computer Architecture
search_query: fetch decode execute cycle instruction set architecture addressing modes

intro.en: The instruction set architecture (ISA) is the contract between software and hardware: it lists the instructions a CPU understands. The CPU runs them one after another in the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
intro.ru: Instruction set architecture (ISA) software aur hardware ke darmiyan muahida hai: is mein woh instructions hain jo CPU samajhta hai. CPU inhein fetch-decode-execute cycle mein ek ke baad ek chalata hai.

definition.en: The instruction cycle is the repeated sequence a CPU follows for every instruction: fetch it from memory at the address in the program counter (PC), decode its opcode and operands, execute it (ALU operation, memory access or branch) and write back the result, then move to the next instruction.
definition.ru: Instruction cycle woh dohraya jane wala silsila hai jo CPU har instruction ke liye karta hai: program counter (PC) ke address se memory se instruction lana (fetch), us ka opcode aur operands samajhna (decode), use chalana (execute - ALU operation, memory access ya branch) aur natija likhna (write back), phir agli instruction par jana.

explanation.en: Fetch: MAR <- PC, IR <- Memory[MAR], PC <- PC + instruction size. Decode: the control unit reads the opcode in the instruction register (IR) and selects registers. Execute: the ALU computes, or the address of a load/store is calculated and memory is accessed, or a branch updates the PC. Addressing modes describe where operands come from: immediate (the value is in the instruction), register, direct/absolute (memory address in the instruction), register indirect (address in a register), displacement/base+offset (register + constant, used for arrays and stack variables) and PC-relative (branches). RISC ISAs (ARM, RISC-V, MIPS) use few simple fixed-length instructions and load/store architecture, which is easy to pipeline; CISC ISAs (x86) have many complex variable-length instructions that can access memory directly. In the von Neumann architecture instructions and data share one memory.
explanation.ru: Fetch: MAR <- PC, IR <- Memory[MAR], PC <- PC + instruction size. Decode: control unit instruction register (IR) ka opcode parhta hai aur registers chunta hai. Execute: ALU hisaab karta hai, ya load/store ka address nikal kar memory access hota hai, ya branch PC update karta hai. Addressing modes batate hain operands kahan se aate hain: immediate (value instruction mein), register, direct/absolute (memory address instruction mein), register indirect (address register mein), displacement/base+offset (register + constant, arrays aur stack variables ke liye) aur PC-relative (branches). RISC ISAs (ARM, RISC-V, MIPS) kam, saadi aur ek hi length ki instructions aur load/store architecture istemal karte hain, jinhein pipeline karna aasan hai; CISC ISAs (x86) mein bohat si complex, mukhtalif length ki instructions hain jo seedha memory access kar sakti hain. Von Neumann architecture mein instructions aur data ek hi memory share karte hain.

example.en: MIPS 'lw $t0, 8($s1)' (displacement mode): fetch the instruction at PC and set PC = PC + 4; decode opcode lw, base register $s1, offset 8, destination $t0; execute: address = $s1 + 8; memory: read that word; write back into $t0. If $s1 = 1000, the word at address 1008 is loaded.
example.ru: MIPS 'lw $t0, 8($s1)' (displacement mode): PC wali instruction fetch karein aur PC = PC + 4; decode: opcode lw, base register $s1, offset 8, manzil $t0; execute: address = $s1 + 8; memory: woh word parhein; write back: $t0 mein. Agar $s1 = 1000 ho to address 1008 ka word load hota hai.

subject: Computer Architecture
search_query: instruction pipelining hazards forwarding stalls speedup
video_queries: pipeline hazards data control structural forwarding

intro.en: Pipelining is the assembly-line idea applied to the CPU: while one instruction executes, the next is decoded and a third is fetched. It is the main reason modern CPUs finish about one instruction per cycle.
intro.ru: Pipelining CPU par assembly line ka idea hai: jab ek instruction execute ho rahi ho, agli decode aur teesri fetch ho rahi hoti hai. Jadeed CPUs ke har cycle mein takreeban ek instruction mukammal karne ki asal wajah yahi hai.

definition.en: A pipeline divides instruction execution into stages - classically IF (fetch), ID (decode/register read), EX (execute), MEM (memory access) and WB (write back) - so that several instructions overlap. Hazards are situations that prevent the next instruction from entering the pipeline in the next cycle.
definition.ru: Pipeline instruction ke chalne ko stages mein baantti hai - classic tor par IF (fetch), ID (decode/register read), EX (execute), MEM (memory access) aur WB (write back) - taake kai instructions ek doosre par aa sakein. Hazards woh halaat hain jo agli instruction ko agle cycle mein pipeline mein dakhil hone se rokte hain.

explanation.en: With k stages and n instructions, an ideal pipeline needs k + (n - 1) cycles instead of n x k, so the speedup is n k / (k + n - 1), approaching k for large n. Three kinds of hazards: structural (two instructions need the same hardware, e.g. one memory port), data (an instruction needs a result not yet written - read after write, RAW) and control (the next instruction depends on a branch outcome). Data hazards are reduced by forwarding (bypassing the ALU result directly to the next instruction); a load followed immediately by a use still needs one stall (load-use hazard). Control hazards are handled by stalling, branch prediction (static or dynamic with history tables) or delayed branches. Every stall adds a cycle, so CPI = 1 + stall cycles per instruction.
explanation.ru: k stages aur n instructions ke saath behtareen pipeline ko n x k ki jagah k + (n - 1) cycles chahiye, is liye speedup n k / (k + n - 1) hai, jo bare n par k ke qareeb pohanchta hai. Teen qisam ke hazards: structural (do instructions ko ek hi hardware chahiye, maslan memory ka ek port), data (instruction ko aisa natija chahiye jo abhi likha nahi gaya - read after write, RAW) aur control (agli instruction branch ke natije par munhasir hai). Data hazards forwarding se kam hote hain (ALU ka natija seedha agli instruction ko dena); load ke foran baad istemal ko phir bhi ek stall chahiye (load-use hazard). Control hazards stall, branch prediction (static ya history tables wala dynamic) ya delayed branches se sambhale jate hain. Har stall ek cycle barhata hai, is liye CPI = 1 + har instruction ke stall cycles.

example.en: 5-stage pipeline, 100 instructions, no hazards: 5 + 99 = 104 cycles versus 500 without pipelining, speedup 500 / 104 = 4.81. If 20% of instructions are loads and half of them are followed by a dependent instruction (1 stall each), CPI = 1 + 0.2 x 0.5 x 1 = 1.1.
example.ru: 5-stage pipeline, 100 instructions, koi hazard nahi: 5 + 99 = 104 cycles, pipelining ke baghair 500, speedup 500 / 104 = 4.81. Agar 20% instructions loads hon aur un mein se aadhi ke foran baad dependent instruction ho (har ek par 1 stall), to CPI = 1 + 0.2 x 0.5 x 1 = 1.1.

title.en: Cache Memory and the Memory Hierarchy

subject: Computer Architecture
search_query: cache memory mapping direct mapped set associative hit miss
video_queries: cache memory mapping direct mapped set associative explained
memory hierarchy locality of reference cache

intro.en: Main memory is about 100 times slower than the CPU. Caches - small, fast memories close to the CPU - hide most of that delay by keeping recently used data nearby.
intro.ru: Main memory CPU se takreeban 100 guna dheemi hai. Caches - CPU ke qareeb chhoti, tez memories - haal mein istemal hua data paas rakh kar is der ka zyada tar hissa chhupa dete hain.

definition.en: A cache stores copies of memory blocks. An address is split into tag, index and block offset; the index selects a cache line (or set), the tag identifies which memory block is stored there, and a hit means the data is found in the cache. Mapping can be direct-mapped, set-associative or fully associative.
definition.ru: Cache memory blocks ki copies rakhta hai. Address tag, index aur block offset mein toot-ta hai; index cache line (ya set) chunta hai, tag batata hai wahan kaunsa memory block rakha hai, aur hit ka matlab data cache mein mil gaya. Mapping direct-mapped, set-associative ya fully associative ho sakti hai.

explanation.en: Caches work because of locality: temporal (recently used data is used again) and spatial (nearby addresses are used soon). The memory hierarchy goes registers -> L1 -> L2 -> L3 -> main memory -> disk, each level larger and slower. For a cache of C bytes with blocks of B bytes and associativity A: offset bits = log2 B, number of sets = C / (B x A), index bits = log2(sets), tag bits = address bits - index - offset. Direct-mapped (A = 1) is simple and fast but suffers conflict misses when two blocks map to the same line; set-associative caches reduce conflicts and use a replacement policy (LRU) inside each set. Misses are compulsory (first access), capacity (cache too small) or conflict. Average memory access time AMAT = hit time + miss rate x miss penalty. Writes use write-through or write-back (with a dirty bit).
explanation.ru: Caches locality ki wajah se kaam karte hain: temporal (haal mein istemal hua data dobara istemal hota hai) aur spatial (qareebi addresses jaldi istemal hote hain). Memory hierarchy registers -> L1 -> L2 -> L3 -> main memory -> disk hai, har level bara aur dheema. C bytes ke cache, B bytes ke blocks aur associativity A ke liye: offset bits = log2 B, sets ki tadaad = C / (B x A), index bits = log2(sets), tag bits = address bits - index - offset. Direct-mapped (A = 1) saada aur tez hai lekin jab do blocks ek hi line par map hon to conflict misses hote hain; set-associative caches conflicts kam karte hain aur har set ke andar replacement policy (LRU) istemal karte hain. Misses compulsory (pehli rasai), capacity (cache chhota) ya conflict hote hain. Average memory access time AMAT = hit time + miss rate x miss penalty. Writes write-through ya write-back (dirty bit ke saath) istemal karte hain.

example.en: 32-bit addresses, 64 KB direct-mapped cache, 16-byte blocks: offset = log2 16 = 4 bits, lines = 65536 / 16 = 4096, index = 12 bits, tag = 32 - 12 - 4 = 16 bits. With hit time 1 ns, miss rate 5% and miss penalty 100 ns: AMAT = 1 + 0.05 x 100 = 6 ns.
example.ru: 32-bit addresses, 64 KB direct-mapped cache, 16-byte blocks: offset = log2 16 = 4 bits, lines = 65536 / 16 = 4096, index = 12 bits, tag = 32 - 12 - 4 = 16 bits. Hit time 1 ns, miss rate 5% aur miss penalty 100 ns ke saath: AMAT = 1 + 0.05 x 100 = 6 ns.

title.en: CPU Performance, CPI and Amdahl's Law
title.ru: CPU Performance, CPI aur Amdahl's Law

subject: Computer Architecture
search_query: cpu performance equation cpi clock rate amdahl's law
video_queries: CPU performance equation CPI clock rate computer architecture

intro.en: Is a 3 GHz processor always faster than a 2 GHz one? Not necessarily. The CPU performance equation shows how clock rate, instruction count and cycles per instruction work together.
intro.ru: Kya 3 GHz processor hamesha 2 GHz se tez hota hai? Zaroori nahi. CPU performance equation dikhati hai ke clock rate, instruction count aur cycles per instruction mil kar kaise kaam karte hain.

definition.en: CPU time = instruction count x CPI x clock cycle time = instruction count x CPI / clock rate. CPI is the average number of clock cycles per instruction. Amdahl's law gives the overall speedup when only a fraction f of the execution is sped up by a factor s: speedup = 1 / ((1 - f) + f / s).
definition.ru: CPU time = instruction count x CPI x clock cycle time = instruction count x CPI / clock rate. CPI har instruction ke average clock cycles hain. Amdahl's law batata hai jab chalne ke waqt ka sirf hissa f, s guna tez ho to kul speedup kitna hoga: speedup = 1 / ((1 - f) + f / s).

explanation.en: Instruction count depends on the program, compiler and ISA; CPI on the microarchitecture (pipeline, caches) and instruction mix; clock rate on technology and design. With an instruction mix, CPI = sum over classes of (fraction x CPI of the class). Performance = 1 / execution time, and 'A is n times faster than B' means time_B / time_A = n. MIPS = instruction count / (time x 10^6) is misleading across ISAs. Amdahl's law shows the limit of improving one part: if 80% of the time is sped up infinitely, the total speedup is at most 1 / 0.2 = 5. It also limits parallel speedup on p processors: 1 / ((1 - f) + f / p).
explanation.ru: Instruction count program, compiler aur ISA par munhasir hai; CPI microarchitecture (pipeline, caches) aur instructions ke mix par; clock rate technology aur design par. Instructions ke mix ke saath CPI = har class ke (hissa x us class ka CPI) ka sum. Performance = 1 / execution time, aur 'A, B se n guna tez hai' ka matlab time_B / time_A = n. MIPS = instruction count / (time x 10^6) mukhtalif ISAs mein gumrah kun hai. Amdahl's law ek hisse ko behtar karne ki had dikhata hai: agar 80% waqt la-mehdood tez ho jaye to bhi kul speedup zyada se zyada 1 / 0.2 = 5 hai. Yeh p processors par parallel speedup ki had bhi batata hai: 1 / ((1 - f) + f / p).

example.en: Program: 10^9 instructions, CPI 2, clock 2 GHz -> time = 10^9 x 2 / (2 x 10^9) = 1 s. Instruction mix 50% ALU (CPI 1), 30% load/store (CPI 2), 20% branch (CPI 3): CPI = 0.5 + 0.6 + 0.6 = 1.7. If 80% of the time is made 4 times faster: speedup = 1 / (0.2 + 0.8 / 4) = 1 / 0.4 = 2.5.
example.ru: Program: 10^9 instructions, CPI 2, clock 2 GHz -> time = 10^9 x 2 / (2 x 10^9) = 1 s. Instructions ka mix 50% ALU (CPI 1), 30% load/store (CPI 2), 20% branch (CPI 3): CPI = 0.5 + 0.6 + 0.6 = 1.7. Agar 80% waqt 4 guna tez ho jaye: speedup = 1 / (0.2 + 0.8 / 4) = 1 / 0.4 = 2.5.
